subject: literature
passage: Every autumn a man from the canning company drove out to make my aunt an offer for the orchard, and every autumn she walked him to his car without giving an answer. The trees were old and crooked, and half the apples fell before anyone could pick them. When I asked her why she did not simply sell the land and move into town, she looked at me as if I had asked why she did not sell her own ______ she said finally, "has been something I did not plant." The next spring she taught me to graft a new branch onto an old trunk.
stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

explanation.why: The sentence about the aunt's look ends at "hands," so a period is needed there. The quotation "Nothing here … has been something I did not plant" is interrupted by "she said finally," and an interrupting attribution is set off by commas. In American English the comma goes inside the closing quotation mark.
explanation.A: Correct. The period ends the previous sentence, and the comma inside the quotation marks separates the first part of the quotation from "she said finally."
explanation.B: Incorrect. A comma after "hands" joins the narrator's sentence to the quotation with nothing but a comma, creating a comma splice.
explanation.C: Incorrect. When an attribution such as "she said" interrupts a quotation, a comma must separate the quoted words from it.
explanation.D: Incorrect. In American English, a comma that follows quoted words is placed inside the closing quotation mark, not after it.
